official.deadline_note: There is no central deadline: the scholarships are awarded by the universities, which publicly advertise them and set their own application procedure and dates.
official.application_cycle: Ongoing national programme running since the summer semester 2011, anchored in the Stipendienprogramm-Gesetz without time limitation; scholarships are awarded by the participating universities.
official.status_note: The programme is introduced without time limitation and universities award scholarships on an ongoing basis.
benefits: 300 euros per month: 150 euros from a private sponsor (companies, foundations, alumni or private individuals) matched by 150 euros from the Federal Government
The scholarship is awarded without consideration of personal or parent income and can be combined with BAföG without restriction
Scholarship funds do not count towards BAföG grants, and there are no social insurance contributions payable
Many universities and private sponsors also provide non-financial support: mentoring programmes, networking events and internships
Paid out directly by the university to the scholarship holder
eligibility: Enrolled at a public or state-recognised university in Germany
First- and higher-semester students of all nationalities can apply
Nationality is not material to the award and there is no income test
Previous career expected to show outstanding study performance
Consideration of overcoming particular biographical hurdles arising from family or cultural background
Applicants must meet the requirements of the individual institution
requirements: Each university publicly advertises the scholarships it awards and defines its own application procedure and documents
Selection decisions are made by the universities; for part of the scholarships sponsors can make a binding determination of the subject of study
selection_criteria: Academic achievement: particular successes at school and/or university
Overcoming particular biographical hurdles arising from family or cultural background
Sponsors of individual scholarships may fix the subject of study; representatives of private funders may sit on selection committees in an advisory capacity
coverage: 300 euros per month, paid monthly directly by the university; granted income-independently and in addition to BAföG
Non-financial support from universities and sponsors (mentoring, networking, internships) where offered
application_method: The Deutschlandstipendium is awarded by the universities; applicants apply directly to their own university and must meet that institution's requirements
official.application_route: Apply directly to your own participating German university, which runs its own advertised selection process; there is no central application portal.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students of all nationalities; award made without regard to nationality or income.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - first- and higher-semester students of all nationalities at participating German universities can apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No central subject requirement; individual private sponsors may tie particular scholarships to a specific subject of study.
official.duration: Normally at least two semesters, and at most until the end of the standard period of study; the university reviews every two semesters whether the holder still meets the criteria and whether private funding continues.
official.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is Germany's national public-private scholarship: private sponsors pledge 150 euros a month and the Federal Government matches it with another 150, so talented and committed students at participating universities receive 300 euros a month regardless of income or nationality.
official.program_type: Public-private partnership scholarship (Federal Government plus private sponsors, awarded by universities)

study_mode (not published on the official pages)

central list of required application documents (each university defines its own)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a top-up, not a full scholarship: EUR 300 a month on top of whatever else you have, so keep your BAföG, job or family support as your main funding. There is no national application form or deadline - your university advertises its own calls, advertises the scholarship itself, decides, and pays the money monthly. Grades alone will not carry the application, because the published criteria explicitly weigh social commitment and having overcome personal or family obstacles. If you win, the value often extends beyond the cash through sponsors' mentoring, internships and networks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled students at participating German universities, including international students already holding a place, with strong grades plus visible social engagement or a personal-overcoming story.
application_readiness_checklist: Check that your university actually participates (the site's interactive map lists all providers)
Find your university's own Deutschlandstipendium call and note its deadline, which is set locally and can be months before the semester starts
Assemble the university's own form, a CV and a motivation statement that documents grades, engagement and any hurdles overcome
Line up a professor or advisor reference early - universities decide in selection panels
Prepare for a possible panel interview or presentation, and read up on the sponsor behind the specific scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a national deadline that does not exist and missing the local one
Selling only grades: committees score engagement and overcoming obstacles just as heavily
Applying before enrolment - the scheme supports enrolled students, not applicants to places
Assuming it covers tuition or living costs in full; it is a fixed EUR 300/month top-up
Applying at a university whose sponsor has already fixed the scholarship to a different subject
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition (nothing published as covered), semester contributions, rent, health insurance gaps and any travel; the EUR 300/month supplements but does not replace a main funding source.
document_audit: Do not submit a generic DAAD-style dossier: universities define their own forms and attachments
Your motivation statement must evidence engagement and obstacles, not just list achievements
Keep enrolment proof current - applications hinge on being enrolled at a participating university
alerts: No central deadline exists; each university's date is the only date that matters to you
Universities may award to up to 1.5% of their students (up to 8% where other universities in the state leave quota unused), so competition is campus-level and intake can be tiny
Some calls are subject-restricted by the sponsor, so eligibility can differ between two calls at the same university
Funding is re-checked every two semesters, so continued study performance still matters after you win
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch your university's public call, file its own application form and documents with the scholarship office, await the university's selection decision, then receive EUR 300/month paid by the university for at least two semesters.

official.deadline_note: Deadlines are country-specific for the current cycle (funding start 2027): earliest 31 August 2026 (already passed), then 21 October 2026, 30 October 2026 (USA), 2 November 2026, 16 November 2026 (most countries), 30 November 2026 (e.g. Denmark), 1 December 2026 (e.g. Austria, Poland, the Netherlands). Selections take place February-May 2027 depending on country; the DAAD portal closes at 24:00 CET/CEST on the deadline day.
official.application_cycle: For funding beginning in 2027, usually 1 October 2027 or winter semester 2027/2028; applications are possible from 1 June until the country-specific deadline, with selections February-May 2027.
official.status_note: The current round targets a funding start in 2027; most country deadlines fall between late October and early December 2026, and funding must begin in 2027 (usually 1 October 2027, or earlier with a preliminary German language course).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Please note that the DAAD does not cover tuition fees.
benefits: Scholarship payments of 992 euros a month
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, granted upon application only
Annually a study allowance of 460 euros
After start of funding, on application: monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members; disability-related extra-cost subsidy where justified

Language preparation: course fees for an online language course after the award letter, a German language course of 2, 4 or 6 months before the study stay where needed (compulsory if the programme is taught in German), an allowance for a self-chosen German course, and TestDaF/DSH fee reimbursement
Green Mobility Top Up or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel
eligibility: First degree (e.g. Bachelor's or Diplom) completed at the latest by the time the funding period begins
As a rule the most recent university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline
Application cannot be considered if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
Funding only for degree programmes starting in the winter semester of the following year (2027); not possible for a Master's already begun in Germany
Applicant is responsible for applying for and securing admission to the German host university in time; admission must exist before the funding period begins
requirements: Complete the online application in the DAAD portal during the application period (portal access only appears while the period is running)
Proof of knowledge of the language(s) of instruction of the chosen study programme, normally no older than 3 years
One recent supporting letter of recommendation from a university teacher, generated via the portal form

Study or work placements of several months outside Germany are only funded if essential, outside the home country, and no longer than a quarter of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint/double-degree programmes)
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
Letter of motivation (1-3 pages) with academic and personal reasons for the study project in Germany
Letter of admission to the study programme at the host university in Germany (if not yet available, must be submitted before the funding period begins)
Current transcript of records with individual grades, plus the university degree certificate with final grade(s)
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes' for a full Master's in Germany, or proof of credit recognition by the home university for a study year abroad
Proof of language knowledge of the language(s) of instruction (normally no older than 3 years), plus optional further documents such as employment certificates or proof of extracurricular engagement
selection_criteria: Academic qualification: achievements, school leaving certificate if applicable, course of studies, knowledge of the language(s) of instruction, relevant internships or work experience
Quality of the study project and of the preparation: preliminary information, choice of degree programme, host university, establishment of contacts
Integration of the project into the academic career path

Potential of the applicant: motivation, German language skills if different from the working language, prospects of the stay for further academic, professional and personal development, extracurricular commitment
Reviewed by an independent selection committee of specialist scientists, with due consideration of equal-opportunity aspects
coverage: Monthly scholarship payments of 992 euros for a stay of 10-24 months (standard period of study, maximum 24 months)
Health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance upon application, and an annual study allowance of 460 euros
Language course costs and TestDaF/DSH fee reimbursement as published
Tuition fees are not covered by the DAAD
application_method: Register in the DAAD portal, generate the recommendation form for your university teacher, complete the online application and upload all documents as PDFs, then submit online between 1 June and your country's deadline
official.application_route: Online via the DAAD portal; applications are accepted from 1 June until the country-specific deadline, and the portal only opens during the application period.
official.study_mode: Postgraduate course of study: a full Master's degree programme or one year of study within a second/Master's degree at the home university
official.citizenship_residency: Open to graduates applying from an eligible country and status; your application cannot be considered if you have been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - designed for international applicants applying from outside Germany (country and status must be in the programme's eligible list).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All academic disciplines; applicants from artistic disciplines and architecture including urban design are directed to the separate DAAD Architecture, Fine Art/Design/Film, Performing Art or Music programmes.
official.duration: Between 10 and 24 months depending on the length of the chosen programme; awarded for the standard period of study up to a maximum of 24 months, with academic achievements reviewed after the first year.
official.description: DAAD Study Scholarships fund a full postgraduate or Master's degree programme at a state or state-recognised university in Germany, or one year of study within a degree completed at your home university with credit recognition; funded by the German Federal Foreign Office and awarded for a stay of 10 to 24 months.
official.region: Germany (study destination); applicants apply from eligible countries worldwide
official.program_type: DAAD study scholarship funded by the German Federal Foreign Office
official.english_requirement: Proof of knowledge of the language(s) of instruction of the chosen study programme (German, English, or German and English), normally no older than 3 years. Accepted English proofs include Cambridge English, Cambridge Business, IELTS, ISE, TOEFL iBT, TOEFL Essentials, TOEIC, PTE Academic, onSET English and Duolingo English Test; accepted German proofs include TestDaF, DSH, DSD, Goethe-Zertifikat, Oesterreichisches Sprachdiplom, telc Deutsch and onSET Deutsch. Minimum scores are not published on the programme page.

not_confirmed: A single central deadline (deadlines are published per country in DAAD's scholarship database; 16 November 2026 is the most common for this cycle)
Minimum required English or German test scores (only accepted certificate types are published)
Exact travel allowance amount (set in DAAD's linked travel allowance rates PDF)
research_requirement (the programme requires a letter of motivation about the study project, not a research proposal)
verification.notes: Values (992 EUR/month, 460 EUR/year study allowance, insurance cover, travel allowance on application, no tuition coverage), 10-24 month duration, requirements, documents and selection criteria verified on the official DAAD programme page; country-specific deadlines for funding start 2027 verified in the database's official deadline data.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full living-cost scholarship, not a tuition scholarship: EUR 992 a month plus insurance, a 460 EUR annual study allowance and a travel allowance on request, but the DAAD states plainly that it does not cover tuition fees. The open round funds studies starting in October 2027 and runs from 1 June to a country-specific deadline falling between late October and early December 2026, so your country's date is the first thing to look up. You apply from outside Germany, need a first degree completed within the last six years, and are personally responsible for securing admission to your German university before funding starts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates (degree under six years old) applying from outside Germany for a full Master's in Germany, with a well-prepared study project and a referee who can write a strong supporting letter.
application_readiness_checklist: Look up your country's exact deadline in the DAAD database before doing anything else, and diarise a submission at least a week early
Register on the DAAD portal from 1 June and email your professor the portal-generated recommendation form straight away
Draft the 1-3 page letter of motivation around programme choice, host university and the contacts you have already made
Apply for admission to the German university in parallel - the DAAD award only becomes valid once you are admitted
Scan and translate all documents into German or English PDFs before the window closes, and claim the travel allowance with the application
common_rejection_risks: Submitting on the last day and hitting portal problems - the portal shuts at midnight CET/CEST and technical issues are your risk
Submitting an incomplete file: incomplete applications cannot be considered and you are responsible for completeness
Assuming the scholarship pays tuition - it does not, so a fee-charging programme breaks the budget
Having spent more than 15 months in Germany, or a degree older than six years
A motivation letter that reads as a generic wish list rather than a documented study project with a named host university
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, visa and residence permit costs, any university semester contribution, and the gap before rent or family subsidies (which must be applied for only after funding starts).
document_audit: Certificates in a national language need German or English translations uploaded together with the original
Language certificates should be no older than three years, and must be submitted even if your university does not require them
The admission letter can follow later, but must reach the DAAD before funding begins - a missing admission voids the award
Only PDFs can be uploaded to the portal, and the recommendation must use the portal-generated form, not a free-form letter
alerts: Funding is only possible for programmes starting in the winter semester of 2027/2028, not for a Master's already begun
If your programme is taught in German, a preliminary 2-, 4- or 6-month language course is compulsory and funding may start earlier than October 2027
Rent subsidy, family allowance and disability subsidies can only be applied for after the funding has started
The portal only appears while the application period runs, so prepare all documents before your country opens
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the DAAD portal from 1 June, send the portal-generated recommendation form to your referee, upload CV, motivation, transcripts, degree certificate, language proof and any optional documents as PDFs by your country's deadline, then secure university admission before the funding period begins.
